questions.stem: Which of the following is an arithmetic progression?
questions.explanation: An arithmetic progression has a constant common difference. In $3, 7, 11, 15$ each term is $4$ more than the one before it, so $d = 4$. The others change by doubling, by odd numbers, or by an amount that is not constant.

distractorRationale.a: This is a geometric progression with common ratio $2$
distractorRationale.b: These are square numbers; the differences $3, 5, 7$ are not constant
distractorRationale.d: The differences are $0, 5, 10$, which are not constant

questions.stem: The common difference of the sequence $12, 7, 2, -3, \ldots$ is
questions.explanation: The common difference is any term minus the previous one: $7 - 12 = -5$, and $2 - 7 = -5$. The sequence is decreasing, so $d$ is negative. Dropping the sign is a very common error.

distractorRationale.a: Took the positive gap $5$ and dropped the minus sign
distractorRationale.c: Miscalculated $7 - 12$ as $-4$, or used $12 - 16$
distractorRationale.d: Added the first and last given terms, $12 + 7$

questions.stem: The first term of an AP is $5$ and the common difference is $3$. The 10th term is
questions.explanation: The $n$th term is $T_n = a + (n - 1)d$. So $T_{10} = 5 + 9 \times 3 = 5 + 27 = 32$. Using $n$ rather than $n - 1$ is the standard slip and gives $5 + 10 \times 3 = 35$.

distractorRationale.a: Computed $(n-1)d = 27$ and forgot to add $a$
distractorRationale.b: Computed $nd = 30$ and forgot to add $a$, or used $10 \times 3$
distractorRationale.d: Used $a + nd = 5 + 30 = 35$, forgetting that there are only $9$ steps from the first term to the 10th

questions.stem: Find the sum of the first $10$ terms of the AP $2, 4, 6, 8, \ldots$. Give a number only.
questions.explanation: Here $a = 2$, $d = 2$ and $n = 10$, so the last term is $T_{10} = 20$. Then $S_n = \frac{n}{2}(a + l) = \frac{10}{2}(2 + 20) = 5 \times 22 = 110$. The equivalent form $\frac{n}{2}[2a + (n-1)d] = 5[4 + 18] = 110$ gives the same result.

questions.stem: The $n$th term of an AP is $37$. If $a = 7$ and $d = 5$, the value of $n$ is
questions.explanation: Set $T_n = a + (n-1)d$: $7 + (n-1)5 = 37$, so $(n-1)5 = 30$ and $n - 1 = 6$, hence $n = 7$. Stopping at $n - 1 = 6$ is the usual incomplete step.

distractorRationale.a: Gave $n - 1 = 6$ instead of $n$
distractorRationale.c: Added $1$ twice, using $a + nd = 37$
distractorRationale.d: Stopped after computing $(n-1)d = 30$

questions.stem: The 3rd term of an AP is $11$ and the 7th term is $23$. The 10th term is
questions.explanation: From $a + 2d = 11$ and $a + 6d = 23$, subtract to get $4d = 12$, so $d = 3$. Then $a = 11 - 6 = 5$. Therefore $T_{10} = 5 + 9 \times 3 = 32$. The sequence is $5, 8, 11, 14, 17, 20, 23, 26, 29, 32$.

distractorRationale.a: Added $6d$ to $T_3$ using $6$ steps instead of $7$, giving $11 + 18 = 29$ (which is actually $T_9$)
distractorRationale.c: Used $a + nd = 5 + 10 \times 3 = 35$
distractorRationale.d: Repeated the given 7th term

questions.stem: The 4th term of an AP is $15$ and the 9th term is $35$. Find the sum of the first $10$ terms. Give a number only.
questions.explanation: From $a + 3d = 15$ and $a + 8d = 35$, subtract to get $5d = 20$, so $d = 4$ and $a = 15 - 12 = 3$. Then $S_{10} = \frac{10}{2}[2(3) + 9(4)] = 5[6 + 36] = 5 \times 42 = 210$. Using the last term $T_{10} = 39$ also gives $\frac{10}{2}(3 + 39) = 210$.
